Remarks

This static class is intended to contain a variety of formatting helpers that improve readability and consistency across applications.

ToCompactOrdinalDateTimeRangeString(DateTime, DateTime, bool)

Converts two DateTime values into a compact ordinal date + time range string. Examples:

  • "15th–17th Dec 2025, 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM"
  • "01st–02nd Jan 2026, 10:00 AM – 11:30 AM"
public static string ToCompactOrdinalDateTimeRangeString(DateTime startDateTime, DateTime endDateTime, bool twoDigitDateFormat = true)

Parameters

startDateTime DateTime

The starting DateTime of the range.

endDateTime DateTime

The ending DateTime of the range.

twoDigitDateFormat bool

If true (default), the day will be formatted with two digits (e.g., "01st"). If false, the day will be formatted without leading zeros (e.g., "1st").

Returns

string

A compact string representing the ordinal date + time range.

ToRelativeTime(DateTime)

Converts a DateTime value into a human-readable relative time string.

public static string ToRelativeTime(this DateTime dateTime)

Parameters

dateTime DateTime

The DateTime value to convert. The input is normalized to UTC before comparison.

Returns

string

A string representing the relative time difference between the specified dateTime and the current UTC time. Examples include:

  • "just now"
  • "5 minutes ago"
  • "yesterday"
  • "2 weeks ago"
  • "3 months ago"
  • "2 years ago"

Remarks

This method uses approximate calculations for months and years based on days (30 days ≈ 1 month, 365 days ≈ 1 year). For precise calendar calculations, consider using Calendar methods.
